paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the LORD is the one to ask, and the LORD is the one who gathers. The message starts with rain in springtime, and it says to ask the LORD for it, because He makes the storm clouds (Zechariah 10:1). Idols and diviners offer "empty comfort," and the people end up wandering "like sheep, oppressed for lack of a shepherd" (Zechariah 10:2). Anything that promises you comfort but has nothing behind it is like a dead battery swearing it still has a charge. Nice try, battery!

Now look at who does the rescuing. He doesn't say, "Earn your way back." He says, "I will restore them because I have compassion on them" (Zechariah 10:6). He also says, "I will whistle for them to gather, for I have redeemed them" (Zechariah 10:8). The people are scattered among the nations, and still they "will remember Me in distant lands" (Zechariah 10:9). The LORD does the gathering, so the whole thing rests on Him, not on how well anybody performed.

So what does this mean for you, baker? When you feel scattered, or you're tempted to chase something that only sounds comforting, bring it to the LORD first. His strength is the kind that lasts, and the passage ends with it: "I will strengthen them in the LORD, and in His name they will walk" (Zechariah 10:12). You don't have to hold yourself together. Walk in His name, friend, and let the Shepherd do the shepherding.
